lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Rate of Change and Building Functions
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: composing functions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: For f(x) = x², find the average rate of change from x = 1 to x = 3.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A sequence has g(1) = 6 and g(n) = 2·g(n − 1). Write the explicit form and find g(4).
A venue charges $25 to open plus $4 per attendee. Write C(n) for the total cost of n attendees, then find C(7).
Revenue is R(x) = -5x + 6 and cost is C(x) = 8x. Write the profit function P(x) = R(x) − C(x) in simplest form.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A table records output 24 at input 2 and output 54 at input 4. What is the average rate of change between these readings?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: For f(x) = -1x² − 7x − 4, find the average rate of change from x = -2 to x = -4.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A sequence has g(1) = 7 and g(n) = 2·g(n − 1). Write the explicit form and find g(4).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
